---
title: "M: Musculo-skeletal system"
description: "ATC group M for modellers: four unrelated PD paradigms under one letter, pain endpoints ruled by placebo and dropout, and bone effects that take years."
date: "2026-02-08"
---

Drugs for joint, bone and muscle disease, plus the neuromuscular blockers given under anaesthesia [@sheinerSimultaneousModelingPharmacokinetics1979].
Published models here span a subjective pain score [@mandemaPopulationPharmacodynamicModel1996] and an evoked muscle twitch [@sheinerSimultaneousModelingPharmacokinetics1979].

In 1938 Richard Gill returned from the Amazon with 11 kg of curare, from which Squibb isolated a standardised extract; Harold Griffith and Enid Johnson gave it in the operating room in 1942 [@elsherbiniConnectionHaroldGriffith2024; @griffithUseCurareGeneral1942].

| Level 2 code | Description |
| ---: | :--- |
| M01 | Antiinflammatory and antirheumatic products |
| M02 | Topical products for joint and muscular pain |
| M03 | Muscle relaxants |
| M04 | Antigout preparations |
| M05 | Drugs for treatment of bone diseases |
| M09 | Other drugs for disorders of the musculo-skeletal system |

: ATC M level 2 codes {#tbl-atc-m-lvl-2 tbl-colwidths="[20, 80]"}

## Modelling notes

**Endpoint.**
Each level 2 code brings its own: WOMAC pain in M01 [@wenPlaceboResponseOral2022], serum urate in M04 [@murakiPopulationPharmacodynamicAnalysis2018], bone markers and density in M05 [@wuQuantitativePredictionBone2021], evoked twitch in M03 [@jiReversalRocuroniumInducedIntense2023].

**Pain needs a fitted placebo time course.**
In oral osteoarthritis trials the WOMAC placebo response is large and reaches 90% of its maximum only after 5 to 7 weeks [@wenPlaceboResponseOral2022].
In an acute postoperative model, pain relief was fitted as a function of ketorolac concentration (**E~max~**), a subject random effect and time, the last capturing the waxing and waning of placebo [@mandemaPopulationPharmacodynamicModel1996].

**Gotcha.**
Patients remedicate when relief is insufficient, with a probability driven by the observed level of pain relief and rising with time, and ignoring that informative dropout biases the drug effect [@mandemaPopulationPharmacodynamicModel1996; @bjornsson2015dropout].

**Urate is a turnover problem.**
Serum urate under febuxostat is fitted with an indirect response model [@murakiPopulationPharmacodynamicAnalysis2018]; such a model predicted real-world urate with r = 0.68, rising to 0.77 once comorbidities, eGFR and loop diuretics were accounted for [@hiraiEvaluationPharmacokineticPharmacodynamic2018].

**Bone markers and density are asynchronous.**
Antiresorptives move serum CTX long before bone mineral density, and an indirect response model bridges the lag, predicting later density gain from one year of data [@wuQuantitativePredictionBone2021].

**Relaxants are the effect compartment case.**
Twitch depression lags plasma concentration, and the hysteresis collapses under an effect compartment, as fitted for d-tubocurarine [@sheinerSimultaneousModelingPharmacokinetics1979].

**Easy to overlook.**
For M02 the relevant exposure is local, in skin and synovial fluid, and dermal PBPK is what links measured plasma concentration to that site, so [bioequivalence](/docs/concepts/clinpharm-studies/ba-be/) is argued at the site of action alongside, not instead of, a plasma study [@tsakalozouPhysiologicallyBasedPharmacokinetic2021].

**Mechanistic extrapolation.**
A multiscale model of calcium homeostasis and bone remodelling [@petersonPhysiologicallyBasedMathematical2010] was extended to predict lumbar spine density under denosumab, including the decline after discontinuation [@petersonPredictingNonlinearChanges2012].
For M02, dermal PBPK replaced a comparative clinical endpoint study in an FDA generic approval of topical diclofenac gel [@tsakalozouPhysiologicallyBasedPharmacokinetic2021].
